$comment: AFL API cutover (AFLDB-ISSUE-316): the ONE switch for AFL Tables network fetching. AFL Tables may be fetched only when status is 'active' AND last_season is an integer AND no season in data/reference/seasons.json in_progress_seasons is later than last_season. status 'active' within that bound leaves every path exactly as before. Otherwise every path that contacts afltables.com refuses before it fetches: deploy/afldb-settle-afltables.sh exits 0 with AFLDB_AFLTABLES_RETIRED when the switch is retired (so a timer or start left enabled does nothing) and exits 1 with AFLDB_AFLTABLES_OUT_OF_BOUNDS when an active switch meets an in-progress season beyond last_season or an unreadable register (a misconfiguration, made loud); legacy/offline/tools/rebuild/fitzroy/acquire_core.R --acquire/--probe, legacy/offline/tools/rebuild/afltables/acquire_club_lists.R and legacy/offline/tools/rebuild/afltables/acquire_coaches.py stop with a non-zero exit; and the Super Admin on-demand start (src/lib/acquisition/settle-trigger.ts) returns 'unavailable' without calling systemctl. A missing file, unreadable JSON, any other status value or a missing or non-integer last_season counts as retired (fail closed). Reading AFL Tables data ALREADY STORED (snapshots, the database, import_fitzroy_core.py, settle-afltables.ts over an existing label) is not a network call and is not gated. Retirement is written by tools/db/rollover-season.ts --apply in the same write as the rollover (it refuses unless this file is active with last_season equal to the season being completed), with decision and changed_at; that commit is the reviewed record. Re-activating AFL Tables for a later season means editing BOTH status and last_season: once that season has matches, it is an ownership decision (AFLDB-ISSUE-316 section 7, Recovery).
